correctness.rationale: For the real normalized duality map J(x)_i=|x_i|^(p−2)x_i, the scalar monotonicity inequality (F(u)−F(v))(u−v)≥2^(2−p)|u−v|^p gives ||J(x)−J(y)||_q≥2^(2−p)||x−y||_p^(p−1). The two-coordinate pair (c,s),(c,−s), s=d/2 and c=(1−s^p)^(1/p), attains this sharp coefficient for all d including d=2. Along ||z||≤a≤1/2, second derivative of ||x+tz||_p is in [0,2(p−1)||z||²], so nonnegative Taylor remainder ≤(p−1)a². Subtracting TWO nonnegative remainders incurs only that bound, not twice it. Duality takes sup_z and then inf over pairs. Numerical random tests at p=3.5 and explicit witness checked boundary consistency but are not an infinite-dimensional proof.
